mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 128ti engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 128ti engine replacement typically costs £1,595-£3,500 for a reconditioned or rebuilt B48A20T1 unit supply-only. With supply and fit, expect £2,800-£4,500 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What engine is in the BMW 128ti?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 128ti is powered by a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine with the engine code B48A20T1. It produces 265 hp (195 kW) at 4,750-6,500 rpm and 400 Nm (295 lb-ft) of torque from 1,750-4,500 rpm. This makes it the most powerful four-cylinder engine BMW has ever produced.

Yes - the B48 engine in the BMW 128ti is generally considered one of BMW's most reliable four-cylinder engines. Unlike the earlier N20, the B48 has far fewer reported timing chain issues. Owners report that the F40 generation is well-built and reliable, with no major engine-related systemic problems. Regular maintenance - including oil changes with BMW-approved oil - is key to long-term reliability.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 128ti engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 128ti engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old B48 unit and fitting the replacement.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 128ti and M135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 128ti and M135i use the same B48 engine family, but with different power outputs and drivetrain configurations. The 128ti produces 265 hp and is front-wheel drive with a Torsen limited-slip differential, while the M135i produces 306 hp and is all-wheel drive (xDrive).

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 128ti - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 128ti was launched in late 2020 as the first front-wheel-drive hot hatch from BMW since the 1990s 3 Series Compact. Reviving the legendary 'ti' (Turismo Internazionale) badge, the 128ti was positioned as a more accessible performance alternative to the all-wheel-drive M135i xDrive. It uses BMW's most powerful four-cylinder engine ever - a 2.0-litre turbocharged B48 producing 265 hp, sent to the front wheels via an eight-speed automatic gearbox with a Torsen limited-slip differential. Production ran from 2020 to 2024 across the F40 generation, before the 1 Series moved to the F70 generation.

milestones.description: Late 2020 - B48A20T1, 2.0L turbocharged petrol, 265 hp (195 kW), launched as a standalone model in the F40 1 Series range
128ti continues production; 'ti' decals, 18-inch wheels and passive sports suspension are standard
Minor updates; 128ti remains the front-wheel-drive performance flagship

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 128ti Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 1 Series 128ti is powered exclusively by the B48A20T1 engine - a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder that produces 265 hp and 400 Nm of torque. The B48 is BMW's most advanced four-cylinder petrol engine and is generally regarded as reliable, with far fewer reported issues than the N20 it replaced. The 128ti is a relatively modern car, so major engine failures are uncommon, but like all direct-injection engines, carbon buildup can occur over time. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components and a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - B48 Direct Injection
problems.rootCause: The B48 uses direct fuel injection, which means fuel is sprayed directly into the combustion chamber rather than over the intake valves. As a result, oil vapours from the crankcase ventilation system can accumulate on the intake valves over time, forming carbon deposits. This can restrict airflow and lead to reduced performance, rough idling, and in severe cases, misfires.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting to remove carbon deposits from intake valves
Complete rebuilt unit with new components
repairOptions.longevity: If carbon buildup has caused significant damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2020-2024 BMW 1 Series 128ti is currently valued at approximately £20,000-£28,000 depending on mileage, condition and specification. This places the 128ti firmly in the bracket where a rebuilt engine is a viable investment - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. For well-maintained, lower-mileage examples, a preventative carbon clean is a cost-effective way to maintain performance.
problems.recommendation: The B48 is a reliable engine, and major failures are rare. The best approach is preventative maintenance - use high-quality fuel, ensure regular oil changes with BMW-approved oil, and consider an intake valve cleaning (walnut blasting) around 60,000-80,000 miles to prevent carbon buildup from affecting performance. If you experience rough idling or reduced power, have a diagnostic check performed before assuming the worst.

problems.group: Cooling System & Oil Filter Housing Wear
problems.h4: Cooling System & Oil Filter Housing Wear - B48 Maintenance Points
problems.rootCause: Like many modern BMW engines, the B48 can suffer from coolant leaks around the coolant flange pipe and oil filter housing. These are typically caused by plastic components becoming brittle with age and heat cycling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant flange pipe and seals
Replace oil filter housing gasket and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Address oil leaks before they cause further issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components

problems.recommendation: Cooling system and oil leak issues on the B48 are usually repairable without engine replacement. Regular visual inspections during servicing can catch these issues early. Address coolant leaks promptly to prevent overheating, and fix oil leaks to maintain correct oil pressure.
